title: Prescriptions Refund Schedule: The Non-Controlled Decline Credit
content:
When a patient declines the open owed balance of a Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Non-Controlled Acute Prescription, Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription or Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription class, the non-controlled decline credit is the amount returned by the original payment method.

## Definition

The non-controlled decline credit is the short fill's patient pay multiplied by the owed units being declined and divided by the units the short fill was meant to carry, being its units dispensed plus the owed units, and it is rounded to the nearest cent.

- **The declined balance** is the prescription's most recent owed-balance entry on the fill ledger, and the owed units are the units that entry booked.
- **The short fill** is the fill that entry names; its patient pay and units dispensed are read from the fill ledger.
- **Rounding** is to the nearest cent, once, on the credit as a whole.

## Worked figures (hypothetical short fills)

| Patient pay of the short fill | Units dispensed | Owed units declined | Units the fill was meant to carry | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24.00 | 20 | 10 | 30 | 24.00 multiplied by 10, divided by 30: 8.00 |
| 13.00 | 28 | 2 | 30 | 13.00 multiplied by 2, divided by 30: 0.8667, rounded to 0.87 |
| 45.00 | 60 | 30 | 90 | 45.00 multiplied by 30, divided by 90: 15.00 |

## Points of judgement

**Two owed-balance entries appear on the prescription's history.** The declined balance is the most recent owed-balance entry, and the short fill is the fill it names.

**Is the divisor the prescribed quantity or the units dispensed?** The units the short fill was meant to carry: its units dispensed plus the owed units.
